articles.expand: A hot PPI and a soft CPI is a poor mix for China’s growth outlook. It points to margin compression for manufacturers and weak domestic demand, which weighs on sentiment toward Chinese equities and keeps expectations of policy support alive. For the yuan, softer underlying inflation argues for easier policy at the margin, a mild negative. For the Australian dollar and commodity currencies, the read is mixed: firm producer prices reflect cost pressure rather than a demand-led recovery in China’s appetite for raw materials. articles.title: Markets price three more BoE hikes, but analysts see a shallower path after move to 4%
articles.expand: The gap between futures pricing and analyst expectations is the key tension for UK assets. If the BoE delivers only one more hike, front-end gilt yields have room to fall and the curve could rally, which is why several analysts favour adding duration. For sterling, a shallower path than priced is a mild headwind on rate differentials. Analysts see little chance of the BoE out-tightening its peers, which limits the pound’s upside. articles.title: Erik Thedéen: Simplify banking regulations – without compromising resilience
